govdocs-archive_org-knut-hamsun-wanderer: Knut Hamsun’s Wanderers — in W. W. Worster’s translation — follows the vagabond’s road through Norway. The Nobel laureate’s novel sings of the open air. Its wanderers live close to the soil. The book is a classic of Norwegian literature.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-CIANelsonWillia: This item — William Nelson Resigns as CIA Operations Aide, creator unknown — is a press note. The file belongs to the intelligence archive. Personnel shifts rarely made headlines. The resignation marked an era’s end. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-DavyWilliam_Dav: William Davy’s Friends of Democratic Cuba is a file on the anti-Castro group. Exile groups plotted against Castro for years. The group made headlines. Researchers value such files. The file belongs to the political archive. The item is a fragment of the record.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-FoxWilliam_Fox_: This item — Fox, William — is a National Security Internet Archive file. The file’s full context is unclear. Its subject seems to be the JFK case. The file may hold a clue. Archivists value such fragments. The item is a fragment of the archive.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-GallagherWillia: M. M. Marberry’s What Christian Fronters Do and Say at Secret Meeting covers the far-right group. The Christian Front spread hate in the 1940s. The exposé was brave. The file belongs to the political archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-GuinyardSam_Gui: This statement of Sam Guinyard — Tippit Witnesses, creator unknown — is a witness file. Guinyard saw the Tippit shooting. His words count. Witnesses shape the case. The file belongs to the assassination archive. The item is a fragment of the record.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-LesarJamesHComm: This record of file review — James H. Lesar, U.S. Civil Service Commission — is a personnel file. Lesar was the FOIA lawyer. The review endures. The file belongs to the government archive. The item is a fragment of the record.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-PattersonWillia: This Secret Service memorandum — Information Obtained at the Dallas Office, by SA Patterson — is an agency file. The Service guards the president. The memo may hold a clue. The file belongs to the government archive. The item is a fragment of the record.
life-is-a-dream: Pedro Calderón de la Barca's 1635 masterpiece is the crown of Spain's Golden Age theater. Prince Segismundo, raised in a tower believing himself a beast, is briefly made king — then told it was all a dream. The play asks whether life itself might be a dream, and whether we should act well regardless. Philosophical, poetic, and still performed worldwide.
de-amicitia-scipio-s-dream: Cicero's De Amicitia — on friendship — joined with Scipio's Dream, his soaring vision of the cosmos, in one classic volume. Rome's greatest prose at its most humane and lofty. Essential Latin for every student of the classics. Laelius speaks for friendship; Scipio dreams of the starry heavens.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-st-e: This piece treats St. Emmeram of Regensburg, the Bavarian house of ancient fame. Its library held treasures of the early Middle Ages. George Cyprian Alston gives its story. Old Germany's bookish pride. Its scriptorium saved many a classic from oblivion.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abel-son-of-a: This 1913 reference piece on Abel, son of Adam — the first martyr, slain by Cain. John Tierney gathers scripture and tradition. His blood cried from the ground, says Genesis. A brief entry on a timeless figure. His lamb was the first acceptable offering.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abraham: This 1913 reference article on Abraham — the patriarch, father of the faithful. James Howlett gathers Genesis, tradition, and archaeology. Ur of the Chaldees, the covenant, and Mount Moriah all find their place. The fullest Catholic account of the great patriarch. Three faiths still call him father.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-adam: This 1913 reference piece on Adam — the first man, father of mankind. James Driscoll gathers Scripture, Fathers, and science. Eden, the fall, and the promise fill the entry. Theology's starting point, fully treated. The protoplast in Catholic thought. His rib became Eve, his helpmate.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-adullam: A 1913 entry on Adullam — David's cave of refuge from Saul. Anthony Maas maps its hills and story. Four hundred malcontents gathered there. The cave became a kingdom's cradle. A hiding place in Israel's tale. Its caves still shelter shepherds today.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aelfric-abbot: This 1913 reference article on Aelfric, Abbot of Eynsham — the great Anglo-Saxon homilist. Herbert Thurston honors his English prose. His homilies taught the faith in the mother tongue. Grammar and saints' lives flowed from his pen. England's first prose master.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ahicam: A 1913 entry on Ahicam — the prince who shielded Jeremiah from death. Florentine Bechtel tells his loyal deed. His house sheltered the prophet's friends. One good man in a faithless court. Courage in Judah's last days. His son Gedaliah ruled the remnant.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alan-of-walsi: This 1913 reference article on Alan of Walsingham — the architect of Ely's glorious Octagon. Thomas Poole praises his daring design. The tower fell, and genius rose. England's finest medieval space. A monk with a builder's soul. His lantern lights the fens for miles.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alexander-of-: A 1913 entry on Alexander Neckam — the English scholar of nature's wonders. Johann Peter Kirsch praises his De naturis rerum. He taught at Paris and Oxford. His lore mixed science with marvel. A schoolman with a poet's eye. His bestiary charmed the medieval readers.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-amsterdam: This 1913 reference article on Amsterdam — the Dutch city's Catholic story. Joseph Lins tells of hidden churches. The Reformation drove faith indoors. Attic chapels kept the Mass alive. A church behind the gables. Its Moses church hides a Catholic past. Its Catholics built the new churches.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antoine-frede: A 1913 entry on Frédéric Ozanam — the founder of the St. Vincent de Paul Society. Georges Bertrin honors his charity. His conferences fed the Paris poor. The scholar became the beggars' friend. The lay apostle of charity. His beatification crowned the century.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-assam: This 1913 reference article on Assam — the Indian mission of the tea gardens. Thomas Shahan tells its modern story. The priests followed the planters' road. The hill tribes heard the Gospel. The Church's northeastern frontier. Its Brahmaputra waters the mission fields.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-balaam: This 1913 reference article on Balaam — the prophet of the talking ass. James Howlett unfolds his strange tale. He blessed whom he came to curse. The star prophecy lit his lips. The seer of the Moabite hills. His ass saw the angel first.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-balsam: A 1913 entry on balsam — the fragrant oil of the chrism. Andrew Meehan explains its sacred use. The bishop blesses the holy oils. The confirmand is sealed with its scent. The perfume of the sacraments. Its tree grows in the Arabian hills.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-bedlam: A 1913 entry on Bedlam — Bethlem, the hospital of the mad. James Joseph Walsh tells its long story. The monks of Bethlehem founded its care. The name became the proverb of chaos. Charity's hospital, fame's byword. Its Bethlem Royal still tends the mad.
